Report of the General Manager
Quarterly Audit and Performance Review Report
items.text: Quarterly Audit and Performance Review Report Irella Blackwood, Audit Director, indicated that for FY 2022-23 there have been 39 audits and assessments with 18 completed (46%), 15 in progress (39%), and six upcoming (15%). She noted audits completed and reports issued. Director Blackwood discussed current Board of Supervisors Budget and Legislative Analysis (BLA) audits: (1) Chapter 6 Delegated Authority Procurement Audit (performance audit of SFPUC’s procurement of public works contracts pursuant to the delegated authority under Chapter 6 of the City’s Administrative Code which focused on the prior three fiscal years); (2) BLA Conflict of Interest Audit (performance audit as directed by the Board of Supervisors as to how conflict of interests are managed and prevented); and (3) Recent SFPUC audit activities. Director Blackwood indicated there are 23 open City Services Auditor audits and recommendations and she informed the Commission of those audits that are completing and upcoming. In response to a question from Vice President (VP) Maxwell, Director Blackwood indicated that the Chapter 6 Delegated Authority Procurement occurs approximately every three years. She noted she is working with the Board of Supervisors on overlaps of requested information

items.title: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency Update
items.text: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency (BAWSCA) Update Nicole Sandkulla, BAWSCA CEO provided an update for BAWSCA’s Regional Reliability Roundtable which provided an opportunity for collaboration among interested stakeholders. She discussed goals of the Roundtable and noted the report is available at the following website. CEO Sandkulla indicated four workshops were held between May 2022 and February 2023, each with a different theme (Demystifying the One Water Concept, Regional Partnerships, Identifying Local One Water Projects, and Moving Forward). She stated invitees included a wide range of participants and each workshop featured guest speakers, highlighted a specific topic of interest, included interactive polls, and shared information on planned future projects. She stated identified future projects have the potential to offer added water supply reliability for the region. She concluded with a review of roundtable workshop findings and next steps. Commissioner Stacy thanked CEO Sandkulla for her presentation and collaborative work. She requested clarification on “other” projects which CEO Sandkulla stated is in the report and that she would provide. CEO Sandkulla responded to a question from President Ajami as to whether there were any opportunities or recommendations that came out of discussions with partners during the workshops. Brief discussion ensued

items.title: Public hearing to consider and possible action to adopt revised Rules and Regulations Governing Electric Service (Rules)
items.text: Public hearing to consider and possible action to adopt revised Rules and Regulations Governing Electric Service (Rules) in conformance with the requirements of Charter section 4.104, effective October 22, 2023. The revised version of the Rules replaces in its entirety the original version that the Commission approved in February 2010 as well as amendments approved in November 2015 and May 2017

items.title: Certificate of Acceptance to accept an approximately seven-acre parcel, in fee and at no cost to the SFPUC, for the future site of the new Treasure Island Wastewater Treatment Plant (TI WWTP)
items.text: Authorize the General Manager to recommend that the San Francisco Director of Property execute a Certificate of Acceptance to accept an approximately seven-acre parcel, known as Block/Lot 8928/001, in fee and at no cost to the SFPUC, for the future site of the new Treasure Island Wastewater Treatment Plant (TI WWTP); approve the terms and conditions of the transfer; and authorize the General Manager to execute a 66-year lease with the Treasure Island Development Authority, a California non-profit public benefit corporation, as landlord, to use approximately three acres of land, comprising a portion of Block/Lot 8946/002, at no cost to the SFPUC, for the future development of wetlands appurtenant to the TI WWTP for the final stage of wastewater treatment. Dina Brasil, Right-of-Way Manager reviewed the history of Treasure Island and discussed the Island’s wastewater treatment needs. She stated that the Treasure Island Development Authority (TIDA) is responsible for all utilities on Treasure Island and that the SFPUC provides operations and maintenance services for existing wastewater facilities as the contract operator. The existing facilities do not meet SFPUC standards and the SFPUC is designing and construction a new wastewater treatment plant.
